newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina awaits Paraguay move on Yacyreta sale.
newsitem.headline: Argentina awaits Paraguay move on Yacyreta sale.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem wants to put plans to privatize the Yacyreta hydroelectric dam on hold until Paraguay's Congress moves to approve the sale, a top government senator said Tuesday.

"The president has informed us that he expects a sign from Paraguay," said Augusto Alasino, Senate leader for the governing Peronist Party, quoted by the private DyN News agency. Alasino said that Menem wants at least one chamber of the Paraguayan congress to pass a bill authorizing the sale before Argentina progresses on the issue.
"It is Argentina's intention that until this happens this matter will be left on stand-by," Alasino said.
Alasino's comments came after the sale of the vast dam, a joint-venture between the Argentine and Paraguayan governments, ran further into trouble in Buenos Aires.
Argentina's state auditor late Monday released a report criticizing the privatization plans, which would award the right to sell Yacyret's electricity for 30 years.

The auditing office recommended instead that a private firm be chosen to run Yacyret but that income from the sale of its electricity would be used by the government to pay off the $8.2-billion debt run up during its construction.
But Alasino dismissed the report and said it was biased. "The report is presented with clear political intentions and does not tell all the truth," he said.

The government, which hopes to garner at least $800 million from the privatization, may have already found some obstacles in the Argentine Congress with its plans for Yacyret. A group of Peronist Party legislators said they oppose the sale and top party officials acknowledge the chances of a privatization bill becoming law this year are slim.

The congressmen said they were worried that plans to allow the export of the dam's electricity to Brazil would mean costlier power in Argentina and opposed the government's proposal to condone Paraguay's part of Yacyret's debt.
Members of the opposition Radical Party are vehemently against the sale, and protestors stormed the site in August.
Argentine congressmen opposed to the privatization met with Paraguayan counterparts in Asuncin Monday, and agreed to set up commissions to investigate the issue.

Yacyret, whose first turbines began to generate power in late 1994, has always been controversial. It ran vastly over budget, was the subject of accusations of corruption, and has recently been blamed for the death of large numbers of fish in the Paran River.
